what_it_does: Map at street zoom is now a real neighborhood. Sample parcels and house footprints are laid out along every Columbus street centerline within about 3,900 ft of the park spot, on both sides of each street, with 58-75 ft lots. Seeds are the street name, so the layout never changes. Parcel depth comes from ray-casting to the street behind. Houses have gable or hip roofs lit from the north-west, soft shadows, attached or detached garages and driveways. No parcels are placed along arterials or crossing other streets, and parcels never overlap each other.
The 25 walk homes sit in that same lot rhythm, pinned to their sample points. They are drawn as brighter footprints with a lot outline. Once a door is logged, its roof takes on the outcome color.
Each lot is tinted by the modeled hail field (A.world.hail.at), using the continuous hail-scale color from the tokens. Hail per door comes from NL.homes.

Knocker ring on every walk door: the arc sweep is the door score and its color is the hail at that door. The ring fills with the outcome color once logged. The number is the walk order. The current door gets an orange halo plus a floating tag (address, and the score or the outcome). Click or hover any ring to select that door. A blue P marks the park spot.

Route in walk order: park, then 22 St, Gruenther, 21 St, 40 Ave (legs from NL.walk s and c), drawn 5 ft to the right of travel. It is solid orange with a glow behind you and dashed ahead, and it grows solid (650 ms) as doors get done. Short spurs run from the sidewalk to each door.

Left panel, header: the zone, the park spot, hail (MRMS), storm date (SPC), best time (engine), a 25-segment walk ring colored by outcome, and four counters that roll (Knocked, Talked, Inspections, Come back).

Left panel, current door card: an animated House portrait, the address with a sample tag, the door score ring (engine) and hail at the door (MRMS, 'radar estimate, not confirmed at this address'). Then the 69-1602 legal check as a checkbox using COPY.knock.legal.check, which is recorded per door. Then built year, roof age and owner-lived (each with a sample tag), and the two COPY flags (no soliciting, asked us not to come back).
Left panel, walk list: street by street (22 St, 21 St, 40 Ave) with door dots in walk order and a count per street. Hovering a street name shows from/to and length in feet from NE GIS.
Sticky outcome bar: No answer, Talked, Not interested, Inspection set, Come back later, with keys N T I X B (U = undo) shown as kbd hints; kbd hints are hidden on phones.

Each tap: rings on the map in the outcome color, Sound.knock() if Sound.enabled, then the door is marked. After 260 ms it moves to the next open door, the camera eases there and the door lifts (ring bump plus the tag springs in).

'Inspection set' opens an inline follow-up at the top of the card with 3 time slots on Wed Sep 30 and 'Open in Deal', which sets A.dealHome, emits 'deal:home' and calls A.view.go('deal'). Picking a slot saves it and moves to the next door.

State is saved per viewer in A.store (key knock.walk.v1): outcomes, history, legal checks, flags and chosen slots. Undo restores the previous outcome and flies back to that door. 'Reset walk' needs two taps.

Evening recap in the bottom dock once all 25 doors are done, using COPY.knock.recap. It shows a singular-aware summary, the inspection rate, how many answered doors had the 69-1602 check, and the answer rate against the Funnel benchmark (30%, bench tag). Stats: inspections, come back, said no, follow-ups. Actions: 'Open <first inspection> in Deal' and 'New walk'.

Entrance, which starts when the camera settles on the street (fallback after 3 s): the neighborhood draws outward from the park spot inside a growing circle behind a thin orange front, lot lines first and houses about 220 ft behind. The park pin lands with a ring. The route then draws itself in walk order with a moving head, and doors pop in one by one as the head passes them. Counters roll, then the current door lifts. Esc skips it; with A.still everything is shown at its end state at once.

Performance: the neighborhood is rendered into two cached images while the camera is still. While it moves, tiles outside the view are skipped, and below zoom 16.4 houses are drawn with fewer details. The 'live' flag is on only while something animates, with no loops left running. Every risky step is wrapped in A.safe.
A.knockDemo = {tap(outcome, rank?), select(rank), undo(), reset(), state(), outcomes}.
build.tests: shoot --view knock --theme both --lang both --still: 4/4 ok, no errors, no horizontal scroll. shoot at --w 1280 --h 800 --still and at --w 400 --h 860 --still: ok. Motion shot (--wait 3500) caught the neighborhood partway through drawing in from the park; it was saved as shots/knock-motion-dark-en-1440.png. smoke --view knock: PASS (49 clicks, 0 errors, no horizontal scroll at 1440/1280/400, 0 long rAF). smoke --view knock --motion: PASS (1 long rAF of 79 ms; 3 or more fails). Extra Playwright scripts checked the full flow: keys T, N, then the legal checkbox, then I; the follow-up; picking a slot; finishing the walk to the recap; U undo. Zero console errors. Note: SwiftShader GPU-canvas shoot mode runs about 2 fps and core caps dt at 64 ms, so timelines play about 10x slower in shoot.mjs than on real hardware.
foundation_requests: core.js ui.srcTag has no 'bench' or 'log' keys. Knock builds custom tags with {label, tip}. Adding shared keys 'bench' (from Funnel) and 'log' (the viewer's own log on this device) would keep the tags consistent across views.
World pal (PK in world.js) has no --warn. Knock reads it through A.tok. Adding warn/warnBg to pal would help every view that colors outcomes.

Timeline and ticker clamp dt to 64 ms. In the SwiftShader shoot harness this makes entrance timelines about 10x slower, so motion shots need a longer --wait. A shoot option to advance the clock (or a real-time Timeline mode) would make motion shots deterministic.

COPY.knock.keys says 'Keys 1 to 5 log the door', which conflicts with the tab keys. Knock uses N T I X B and U instead, so that string should be updated in copy.js. COPY.knock.recap.summary also has no singular forms ('1 inspections'); knock patches this locally.
motion_moments: Entrance: the neighborhood draws in from the park spot inside a growing circle behind a thin orange front, with lot lines leading and houses following. The P pin lands with a ring, then the route draws itself in walk order with a glowing head and the doors pop in one by one (outBack) as it passes. Counters roll up, then the current door lifts: halo, ring bump and a tag that springs in.

Each tap: three rings in the outcome color ring out from that door on the map, the door fills, the solid orange route grows to it, the walk ring segment and street dots recolor and the counters roll. The camera then eases to the next door, which lifts, and the new House portrait builds itself.
Inspection set: the follow-up lands at the top of the card with a ring and the panel scrolls it into view.
Walk done: the camera flies back to the whole walk and the recap dock lands, with its stats following in a stagger.
build.for_filthe: Every answered door logs whether the 69-1602 intro was checked, and the recap shows "said first at X of Y". That gives a per-walk compliance record you could later export as legal proof for each sale.

findings.issue: Where two legs share a point, the code that removes the duplicate point (line 276: `legOf[rp.length-1] = li`) hands that point to the next leg. Line 291 then skips any segment whose two ends belong to different legs. So the last segment of 22 St and the whole of 21 St never match a door. Those doors get arc = total (or get clamped to a segment end) and fall back to rank order. I checked the computed order in the page: 22 St doors 8-10 come out as -97.37511, -97.37484, then -97.37539, which walks back west. 40 Ave is numbered 11-13, before 21 St, although NL.walk says 22 St, then 21 St, then 40 Ave. The 12 doors on 21 St are numbered 14-25 by score, so the walker would cross the street back and forth about 12 times. Knock-on effects: logging any one 21 St door fills the whole route solid orange (I screenshotted this at 1 of 25). 'Next' jumps across the street. All 21 St doors pop in together at the end of the entrance instead of as the head passes. Doors 8-10 get long diagonal spurs.
findings.fix: On a duplicate point, just `return` and leave legOf alone. Give each segment the leg of its end point: build a `segLeg[i] = li` array as you push each point with i>0, and test only `legs[segLeg[i]].st === key` (drop the `legOf[i-1] !== legOf[i]` check). Then assert in a dev script that the arc along each street only ever increases in one direction (22 St eastbound, 21 St westbound, 40 Ave northbound) and that doneArc never passes the furthest logged door.

findings.area: Flags: no soliciting / asked us not to come back
findings.issue: The two flags only toggle S.flags and draw a strike on the map. nextOpen() still offers flagged doors as 'Next'. No outcome is logged, and the walk can't reach 25/25 without knocking them. The recap ignores them. COPY's own hint ('A clear no. The door leaves the list.') says the app does something it doesn't. A no-soliciting sign or a request not to return is legal armor: the app should stop sending the knocker to that door.
findings.fix: Treat a flag as a terminal state: store it as S.o[r]='skip' (or have nextOpen and counts respect flags), advance to the next open door, grey the roof and ring on the map, count 'skipped (sign / asked)' in the recap and in 'said first' math, and keep a persistent do-not-knock list keyed by address so a new walk also skips it.

findings.issue: At 1440, in both EN and ES, the 69-1602 box sits flush on (and over) the bottom of the House portrait frame. The portrait's rounded bottom corners are hidden and the 14 px gap is gone. The hail note 'en esta dirección.' touches the box in ES. It reads as a layout bug on the most important card.
findings.fix: Find why the grid row isn't reserving the full height. Likely the stretched .knock-card__pic plus the right column overflowing its row: try align-items:start on .knock-card__hero with aspect-ratio:4/3 on .knock-card__pic, or move the hail note below the hero. Add a check to shoot/smoke that the legal box's top is at least the hero's bottom + 10.

findings.issue: The ES counter 'INSPECCIONES' is cut to 'INSPECCIONE' (nowrap + overflow hidden, no visible ellipsis). In the ES facts row, 'EDAD DEL TECHO 19 años' pushes MUESTRA onto a second line, so the three values (1962 / 19 / Sí) no longer share a baseline and the row looks broken.
findings.fix: Shorten the ES label ('Inspecc.') or let .knock-stats .stat__k wrap to two lines at every width. In .knock-f, put the sample tag on its own line for all three facts (or use align-content:end with the value last) so the values line up in EN and ES.

findings.issue: 'Your walk, in order' (the street-by-street list with door dots, the thing that shows the plan) is below the fold at both 1440x900 and 1280x800, behind the sticky outcome bar. Nobody sees it without scrolling the panel. Meanwhile the 320 px right slot is empty. When the panel scrolls, the header title gets cut hard at the top with no fade.
findings.fix: Move the walk list, and maybe the walk ring, into #slot-right as its own pane, so left = the door and right = the plan. Add a top mask-image fade on the left slot scroller.

findings.issue: When the walk ends, the 'Walk finished' toast lands exactly on the recap's Inspections number (and on 'typical 30%' at 1280) for 2 s, which is the moment the eye goes there. The recap also leaves out COPY.knock.recap.pace/time and the inspection benchmark, which makes it thinner than it could be.
findings.fix: Drop the toast when the dock recap appears (the dock is the message), or anchor it above the dock. Add an 'inspection rate vs Funnel doors_to_qualified_inspection_new_rep (bench)' stat to make the recap denser.

findings.issue: The current-door tag covers neighboring rings (tag for 15 on 21 St hides 18/19). At 400 px the tag and the P pin are clipped at the map's left edge. The score '83' in the map tag has no source. The per-lot hail tint has no legend, and in dark mode it reads as muddy brown ground rather than data.
findings.fix: Flip or offset the tag away from nearby lit rings and the map edges (check the projected bounds). Add a tiny HUD legend chip, e.g. 'Lot tint = modeled hail · MRMS', with a hail-scale swatch. Raise dark-mode fillA a little and shift it cooler so it reads as hail, not soil.

findings.issue: The still-mode smoke test FAILED on my first run: 3 long rAF (52, 52, 73 ms). It passed on the second run with 1 (59 ms). The builder reported 0. lotsCache redraws the whole neighborhood into two full-DPR canvases on every camera settle, resize and theme change. Those canvases are module-level, about 10 MB each at dpr 2, and stay alive after leaving #knock.
findings.fix: Release LC.a/LC.b on exit (width=height=0, key=''). Build the cache over 2 frames, lots then houses, or pad the cached view so small pans reuse it. Re-run smoke 3 times and report the worst run.

findings.issue: The header counter 'Talked / Hablamos' shows c.answered (talked + inspection + not interested + come back). The outcome button 'Talked' means something narrower, so after one 'Inspection set' the Talked counter says 1 while no door is logged as Talked.
findings.fix: Rename the counter 'Answered / Abrieron' to match the recap, or count only talked.

review.best_thing: The deterministic real-street sample neighborhood (lots and lit gable/hip roofs along actual Columbus centerlines) draws in from the park spot, and each roof takes its outcome color as doors are logged. The map shows the evening's results house by house, which is the leap from "HTML stuff" to a product. Also keep the per-door 69-1602 checkbox that rolls up into "said first at X of Y" in the recap. It is real legal armor, not coaching. Legal/copy grep is clean: no insured, licensed, free, deductible, promise or urgency; HMP Siding & Roofing is named in the 69-1602 check; sample tags are on every home fact.
